title: Measurement-induced phase transition in space
authors: Jia-Qiang Li, Liang-Jun Zhai, Shuo Liu, Shuai Yin
abstract: Measurement-induced phase transitions (MIPTs) in monitored quantum circuits are usually characterized by preparing steady states at different uniform measurement probabilities. Here we introduce a spatial realization of the MIPT by imposing a deterministic measurement gradient in a single monitored Clifford chain. The resulting steady state contains coexisting volume-law, critical, and area-law regions, with the point $p(x)=p_c$ acting as a spatial critical cut. By scanning entanglement observables across this profile, we show that the transition is organized by a spatial scaling form. Although this structure is analogous to finite-time scaling in temporally driven MIPT, the spatial protocol has no Kibble-Zurek dynamics. Instead, the physical bounds $0\le p\le 1$ impose a finite linear window, producing cutoff-controlled asymptotic regimes whose fitted exponents provide direct access to the correlation-length exponent $ν$. Our results establish spatially inhomogeneous measurements as a controlled route to engineer and probe measurement-induced criticality within a single steady state.
summary: This work introduces a spatial realization of Measurement-induced Phase Transitions (MIPTs) in a monitored quantum circuit by imposing a linear gradient on the measurement probability. By analyzing entanglement scaling across this gradient, the authors show that the transition is governed by a specific scaling form. This method allows for the controlled probing and direct calculation of critical exponents within a single steady state.
main_problem: The paper investigates Measurement-induced Phase Transitions (MIPTs) by realizing the transition spatially rather than through uniform measurement probabilities or temporal driving.
main_result: It establishes that a deterministic spatial gradient in measurement probability creates coexisting volume-, critical, and area-law regions within a single steady state, allowing for the direct extraction of the correlation-length exponent $\nu$.
method: The analysis involves scanning entanglement observables (like subsystem entropy) across the spatially varying measurement profile and performing scaling analyses.
model_or_system: The system is a monitored Clifford chain (1+1)D random circuit model where local projective measurements are performed after each gate layer, controlled by a linear gradient $p(x)$.
key_observables: Subsystem entanglement entropy ($S_A$), ancilla entropy ($S_Q$), and tripartite mutual information ($I_3$).
important_parameters: The critical measurement probability $p_c$, the spatial gradient parameter $R$, and the physical bounds $0 \le p(x) \le 1$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on truncating the linear gradient due to the physical constraints of probabilities ($0 \le p(x) \le 1$).
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically shows the circuit and the resulting entanglement structure (Volume-law $\leftarrow$ Criticality $\rightarrow$ Area-law). Figure 3 verifies data collapse for scaling forms on both volume-law and area-law sides.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the spatial MIPT concept, analyzes the steady state containing coexisting regimes via entanglement observables, derives a spatial scaling form analogous to finite-time scaling but without Kibble-Zurek dynamics, and uses this structure to extract $\nu$ from the finite linear window.
why_interesting: It provides a novel, controlled method—spatial inhomogeneity—to engineer and probe measurement-induced criticality within a single steady state, offering insights into non-equilibrium critical phenomena.
